inputs.net_debt_basis: cash-only (no bank debt); lease liabilities excluded from the EV bridge because owner FCF is already stated AFTER lease principal repayments (see fcf_adjustment) -- treating leases as debt in net_debt AND deducting lease principal from FCF would double-count the lease obligation
inputs.normalized_owner_fcf_note: FY2024 owner FCF (pre-DC-capex-surge) shown for reference; FY2025/FY2026 owner FCF is trough-depressed by the Drury DC build (~$50-58m capex vs ~$15-20m maintenance level). The DCF base year for projections is FY2026 revenue with a component build, NOT a flat extrapolation of the depressed FY2026 owner FCF.
inputs.sbc_source: BGP.NZ_Metrics.csv StockBasedComp column / kpis table; SBC is immaterial for this company (never exceeded $0.57m historically)
inputs.fx_note: NZD reporting currency; NZ$4.60 quote from Yahoo Finance BGP.NZ

kmd_brands_stake.note: Briscoe holds a 6.75% equity stake in NZX/ASX-listed KMD Brands, fair-valued at $13.2m at FY2026 year-end (25 Jan 2026), already recognised within Shareholders' Equity/Total Assets on the balance sheet via FVOCI. Not separately added to the DCF equity bridge to avoid double-counting book equity; treated as immaterial (~1.3% of market cap) non-operating asset embedded in net assets.

fcf_adjustment.methodology: IFRS-16 lease adjustment (company-specific): Briscoe's TotalDebt from FY2020 onward is entirely lease liabilities (zero bank debt). Operating cash flow is stated post-IFRS16 (lease interest already in P&L, but LEASE PRINCIPAL repayments sit in financing activities, not operating). Reported FCF (OCF - capex) therefore OVERSTATES owner FCF by the amount of annual lease principal repayments. Owner FCF = reported FCF - lease principal repayments - interest income (net cash > 1x FCF base, so interest income is stripped per the standard adjustment rule).
fcf_adjustment.lease_principal_source: Cash flow statement, financing activities, 'Lease liability payments' line, BGP.NZ_Annual_FY20xx.txt (figures in filing thousands, converted to millions)
fcf_adjustment.ev_bridge_consistency: Net debt uses cash-only (no bank debt) because owner FCF is already net of lease principal; this avoids double-counting the ~$276m lease liability both as a subtracted EV item AND as an annual cash outflow already embedded in the FCF projection.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: component build (revenue growth 1.0-2.5% base case, NOT a single blended CAGR) -- historical CAGRs are all negative or near-zero because FY2023-FY2026 revenue is flat (~$785-799m) while margins compressed and DC capex spiked FY2025-26; none of the trailing CAGRs are usable growth inputs for a mature, no-growth retailer
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: EPS 3yr CAGR (-12.5%) and reported/owner FCF 3yr CAGR (-26% / -35%) diverge sharply from flat revenue (+0.55%) and roughly flat equity (-0.3%). This is NOT a business-model breakdown -- it reflects (a) gross margin compression from 44.0% (FY2023) to 39.2% (FY2026) amid promotional competition, and (b) FY2025-26 capex more than tripling for the Drury DC build, mechanically crushing reported and owner FCF even as revenue and book equity held roughly flat. The DCF therefore does NOT extrapolate any of these trailing FCF/EPS CAGRs -- it builds forward FCF from EBITDA-margin recovery assumptions and a capex normalization glide path back to ~$18-20m/yr maintenance levels once the DC completes (~FY2027-28).
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF CAGR is more negative than reported FCF CAGR (-34.8% vs -26.0% over 3yr) because lease principal payments grew modestly (FY2023 $19.1m -> FY2026 $19.4m) while interest income also declined ($2.5m -> $3.0m, noisy) as reported FCF collapsed on the capex spike -- the lease deduction is a stable ~$19-20m/yr drag, not itself a growth driver of the divergence; the divergence is entirely capex- and margin-driven.

base.rationale: Revenue: FY2027 guided ~flat (Q2 FY2027 trading update +0.25% sales); modest acceleration to 2.5%/yr as DC-driven availability/replenishment gains and gradual NZ consumer/housing normalisation take hold, still well below the FY2021-22 COVID boom growth. EBITDA margin: recovers from FY2026's 16.5% trough (post six years of gross-margin erosion, 45.8%->39.2%) toward a 19.0% mid-cycle target by Y5 -- below the FY2022 COVID peak of 22.75% and below the pre-margin-compression FY2020 level of 19.1%, reflecting a structurally more competitive/promotional NZ retail market that is not expected to fully unwind, but assuming the Drury DC automation delivers the inventory/availability/productivity gains management is guiding toward. Capex: FY2027 guided ~$57m (DC completion year), stepping down as the build finishes (handover Apr-2026, automation complete Sep-2026, ramp-up Q4-2026) to a $18m/yr maintenance level by Y4-Y5, close to the FY2023/24 pre-DC actual of $15-16m plus a modest allowance for the ongoing store refurbishment programme and new $30m trade-finance facility drawdown. Lease principal: modest step-up from $19.4m (FY2026) toward $22m/yr reflecting the new Drury facility lease plus ordinary store network growth. Working capital: -10% capture on revenue growth (a retailer needs incremental inventory to fund growth -- cash outflow, not a deferred-revenue tailwind as in subscription businesses).

bull.rationale: DC automation benefits materialise faster and more fully than base case (margin approaches, but does not exceed, the FY2022 COVID peak of 22.75% by Y5); Rebel Sport captures outsized share from Commonwealth Games/football World Cup cycle and the Rebel X flagship rollout; NZ consumer confidence, interest rates and housing market recover meaningfully, driving above-trend homeware demand; online penetration continues to scale efficiently. Lower WACC reflects reduced execution-risk premium once the DC transition is de-risked.

bear.rationale: Prolonged NZ consumer and housing downturn (real sales volumes already contracting per Aug-2026 management commentary); gross margin keeps eroding on sustained promotional intensity from Warehouse/Kmart/online entrants rather than stabilising; Drury DC benefits are delayed or disappoint, with capex overruns (FY2027 guide of ~$57m proves conservative) and the new trade-finance facility signalling funding strain; dividend cut (20.0cps FY2026 vs 22.5cps FY2025) continues as 60%-of-NPAT policy bites on lower profit. Higher WACC reflects both cyclical/consumer-discretionary risk and execution risk crystallising together.

wacc_rationale.methodology: CAPM build-up + illiquidity/control premium; no separate debt weighting because Briscoe carries zero bank debt (IFRS-16 lease liabilities are treated as an operating obligation embedded in owner FCF, not as financial leverage in the WACC).
wacc_rationale.beta_rationale: Discretionary consumer retailer (cyclical exposure to housing/consumer confidence) but debt-free balance sheet with $130m+ cash materially reduces financial risk versus leveraged retail peers (e.g., The Warehouse Group), holding beta below 1.0
wacc_rationale.illiquidity_control_premium_rationale: Rod Duke controls ~77-81% of shares outstanding; free float is only ~19-22%, thin trading liquidity, and minority shareholders have no practical influence over capital allocation (dividend policy, KMD stake, DC investment decisions all set unilaterally by the controlling shareholder/MD) -- standard small-cap/controlled-company premium applied

base.exit_multiple_sanity_check: Current EV/owner-FCF on FY2026 (DC-capex-depressed) is ~30x, but on FY2024 pre-DC normalized owner FCF (~$82.6m) is ~10.8x. The base case implied exit multiple of 12.8x is a modest premium to the normalized current multiple, consistent with margin recovery from DC benefits rather than aggressive multiple expansion.

base.note: Entry price sits modestly below both current price ($4.60) and base intrinsic value ($4.76), consistent with base-case growth (~1-2.5%) being well below the 15% IRR hurdle -- a buyer needs a discount to today's price to clear 15% given the low organic growth and terminal-value-dominated payoff (74% of EV).
base.entry_price_correction_note: Terminal value rebuilt at the hurdle rate 2026-09-01: min(Gordon@hurdle, cap x FCF_N). The superseded value held the WACC-built terminal value and varied only the discounting.

sensitivity.notes: At 8.5% WACC the Gordon Growth terminal value exceeds the 14x cap across the entire terminal-growth range tested, so all five cells in that row are bound by the cap (identical $5.44 value) -- this correctly flags that low-WACC scenarios are terminal-multiple-capped rather than growth-sensitive.

dividend_context.note: Dividend payer, not a growth stock -- FY2026 total dividend 20.0 cps (cut from 22.5 cps FY2025) on a 60%+ of NPAT payout policy. Included here for context only; the DCF values the enterprise on owner FCF, not a dividend-discount model, since Briscoe retains and reinvests a meaningful share of earnings into the Drury DC programme.

key_watch_items: Drury DC practical completion (end Apr-2026) and automation ramp-up (Sep-Dec 2026) -- the central swing factor for whether base-case EBITDA margin recovery (16.8% -> 19.0%) materialises

Gross margin trajectory -- H1 FY2027 guided a further ~57bps decline (an improvement on the prior year's 115bps decline); a sustained flattening or reversal would support the base/bull case, continued erosion would validate the bear case
FY2027 capex actuals vs the ~$57m guide -- any overrun delays the capex normalization glide path central to base-case FCF recovery
NZ consumer confidence, interest rates and housing market activity -- direct read-through to Briscoes Homeware same-store sales
Dividend policy (60%+ of NPAT) -- further NPAT softness would pressure the ~4.3% current yield lower

sanity_check.basis_note: Earnings multiples are SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS - SBC/share; EBITDA - SBC); SBC is negligible for Briscoe (<NZ$0.6m/yr) so these track GAAP closely. EV includes IFRS-16 lease liabilities as debt against post-IFRS16 EBITDA. FY-end prices are the January monthly close matching Briscoe's late-January fiscal year end. These deliberately differ from screener P/E figures.
sanity_check.diagnosis: No trip. Base IV $4.76 implies P/E 18.1x (vs 14.3x avg, threshold 2.0x avg = 28.6x), P/B 3.47x (vs max 4.51x, threshold 6.77x), EV/EBITDA 9.2x (vs max 9.6x, threshold 14.4x). Base upside is only +3.5% with the price at the 43rd percentile of the 10-year range. The implied P/E sits above the historical average because FY2026 earnings are a cyclical trough (NZ-consumer recession + Drury DC costs), consistent with the DCF's mid-cycle recovery assumption rather than peak extrapolation.
